items.name: PhD, Marquette
items.text: Philosophy. My dissertation became the Kierkegaard book; my research was on reflection and how people come to understand things.

items.name: Marquette

items.name: Wright College
items.text: Adjunct instructor at City Colleges of Chicago: intro to philosophy, humanities, ethics, popular culture.

items.name: Illinois State
items.text: Instructional assistant professor of philosophy.

items.name: Miami, emerging tech programs
items.text: Associate director of Miami University’s Master’s in Entrepreneurship and Emerging Technology; designed and taught a graduate course on emerging technology.

items.name: Miami adjunct
items.text: Back at Miami University as an adjunct.

items.name: High schools
items.text: I’m happy to work with schools on how AI and learning fit together, and with students on entrepreneurial skills and what the entrepreneur path actually looks like. It happens about once a semester. If you run a school or a class and that sounds useful, email me.

items.name: Lyceum AI (CEO)
items.text: The EdTech startup I co-founded and ran. We built AI that checks whether people actually understood their training, got it into Fortune 500 companies, and Perceptyx acquired us in March 2026. It lives on as Develop, which is now my day job.

items.name: Develop at Perceptyx
items.text: Principal product manager for Develop, the AI learning product Lyceum built. My day job.

items.name: Sideris
items.text: A tool that helps a church see the gifts its members already have, through a short conversation that each member controls.

items.name: Strategy exercises
items.text: With two friends, I’m building custom strategy exercises for companies: a working model of a real problem your company is facing, run live with your own people in their real roles. We’re early, and looking for the first organization willing to try one.

items.name: SHADE (DARPA)
items.text: Consultant on a $1M DARPA AI grant about games: how people deceive in negotiation, and how an AI might tolerate and use deception in normal human ways.

items.name: Unveiled
items.text: A two-player strategy card game for adult couples. I wanted to design an adult game where choice and autonomy were central, instead of leaving it all to randomness. It plays in about fifteen minutes.

items.name: Precedent
items.text: A digital wargame about kids’ imaginative play. Each level, you make up a new rule to help you beat it, and that rule stays in the game for good. The catch is that the computer gets to use your rules against you in later levels, so you have to be careful what you invent. It’s half wargame, half roguelike, half turn-based tactics, half Calvinball. It’ll be free, in the browser.
items.status: Not online yet. Playtesters wanted once it is.

items.name: Board games
items.text: Always Dune (the GF9 edition). Lately also Wingspan Pocket, Old King’s Crown, Lost Ruins of Arnak, Everdell, and Rebirth.

items.name: Rocks
items.text: My father was a geologist, and I grew up admiring his rock collection. I’m not sure where most of his rocks came from, though I know he collected some of them in college. Most of mine I’ve bought, with a few lucky finds. Lately I’ve been getting my daughter into rocks too, and we have a tumbler where I mostly fail at making rocks pretty enough for her to turn into jewelry.
items.status: I can’t identify most of them. Help welcome.
